messages:
dina: FYI opened a focused PR to standardize streaming + pagination snippets across py/ts/go. Goal: demonstrate cancel, show minimal retry config, and a tiny note on saving/resuming with the opaque cursor token. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5188

rob: Nice. Please make the examples very compact (single small block each) so they render cleanly in the handbook. Also update any 'resume_token' wording -> 'cursor'.

anya: I'll author the Python and Go snippets. Quick question: prefer `cursor=None` in Python and `Cursor:""` in Go? That matches other recent examples.

sam: Docs convention: Python uses None, TS uses null, Go uses empty string. Add a one-liner under each snippet: "Cursor is opaque; store and pass back unchanged."

dina: Drafts below — intentionally tiny. Feedback welcome.

DRAFT - python:
```python
from redwood import Client
c = Client()
for ch in c.stream('gpt-medium', prompt='brief', max_tokens=40, cursor=None, retry={'strategy':'exp','max_attempts':2}):
  print(ch.text)
```

DRAFT - typescript:
```ts
const ac=new AbortController(); setTimeout(()=>ac.abort(),1200)
for await(const p of client.stream('gpt-medium',{prompt:'brief',maxTokens:40,cursor:null,signal:ac.signal,retry:{strategy:'exp',maxAttempts:2}})) console.log(p.text)
```

DRAFT - go:
```go
ctx,cancel:=context.WithTimeout(context.Background(),1500*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
iter:=client.Stream(ctx,"gpt-medium",redwood.StreamOpts{Prompt:"brief",MaxTokens:40,Cursor:""})
for iter.Next(){fmt.Println(iter.Current().Text)}
```

ci-bot: lint: please use `max_tokens` in Python snippet; fixed Go import to `github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go` if needed.

anya: I'll switch the Python param name and add the one-line note below each block. I'll also add a GH Action `examples-smoke-test` to run these three snippets under an env guard and skip when creds are missing.

sam: Great. Once smoke CI passes I'll approve/merge. Thanks all.
